source: Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab · MIT CSAIL
hook: Can an AI read another AI's weights, and rewrite them, with no training? New research says: sometimes, yes.

beats.label: Exp 1 · 17,253 weights as text
beats.say: First, reading. The researchers trained four small game-playing networks, all the same shape. Given only the raw weights, {GPT-6 Astra|G P T six Astra} named every game.

scene.note: Green: Astra's answer and confidence · no game names were given · clips: the authors' blog post

beats.label: Exp 2 · three diffusion models
beats.say: It also named the shape each of three image models draws. It drew them as outlines, though the models make filled shapes.

scene.note: Top: what the models generate (filled) · bottom: what Astra described (outlines) · redrawn

beats.label: Exp 3 · middle layers only
beats.say: From only the middle layers of three small language models, it named each training language, and found every copying head.

scene.note: Rows: layers 0–3 · columns: heads 0–5 · green: copying heads Astra named, all matching the measured ones

beats.label: Exp 7 · Gemma 3 270M pairs
beats.say: But from weights alone, it could not spot which model was sycophantic. Given attention patterns as well, it found the sycophant in all three pairs.

beats.label: Exp 4 · 3.5% of weights edited
beats.say: Next, fixing. A trained car network always stalled on a ramp. One edit to 3.5 percent of its weights made it succeed in all 1,024 episodes.

scene.note: Scene from the authors' blog post · Kinetix car-on-ramp level

beats.label: Exp 5 · networks written from scratch
beats.say: Then, writing. With no data and no training, it wrote game networks that beat P P O trained for 100 million steps. Against longer training, it won only in Breakout.

scene.note: Average score over 1,000 episodes · bars scaled within each game

beats.label: Exp 6 · 9×9 Go, from zero
beats.say: It even wrote a 1.5 million weight Go network. With 50 test runs, it beat a same-size network trained on 20 million games.
beats.src: Experiment 6; gohand/gohand.json (win rates vs the two small PPO networks)

scene.note: Win rate (%) against two small PPO networks · board is an illustration

beats.label: Exp 8 · 131,072 of 0.8B weights
beats.say: Finally, a real language model. Editing 0.016 percent of {Qwen3.5-0.8B|Kwen three point five}'s weights removed its reasoning loops.

scene.note: Qwen3.5-0.8B, 24 layers · edited: 64 MLP output columns in layers 15 and 19

beats.label: MATH-500: 7.9% → 48.1%
beats.say: They report math accuracy rising from 7.9 to 48.1 percent, and instruction following tripling. But it took 50 test runs. With 10 or 25, the gains were small.

scene.note: Base vs edited · authors' reported results, 50 forward passes

beats.label: Control: Gemma 3 270M
beats.say: On a model that does not loop, the edits did not help. The fix unlocked an ability. It did not add one.

scene.quote: “Editing weights could remove an obstacle that hid an ability, but it could not add an ability the model lacked.”

beats.label: Blog post · not peer-reviewed
beats.say: These are early results in a blog post, not a peer-reviewed paper. The full logs are public, so others can check them.

items: Read: games, shapes, languages from raw weights
Fix and write small networks with no training
Real LLM: removed loops, needed 50 test runs
Sycophancy from weights alone; new skills

outro: Source: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming, M I T C SAIL, November {2026|twenty twenty-six}.
